hook.text: You have one genome. But you have hundreds of epigenomes—one for every cell type. Each reads the same DNA differently.

buildup.text: The epigenome is the complete set of epigenetic marks across your genome.

discovery.text: The Roadmap Epigenomics Project mapped epigenomes from 111 human cell types. Each tissue had a unique pattern of marks.

climax.text: The genome is fixed at conception. The epigenome is a living document, edited by experience from womb to grave.

punchline.text: One genome. Hundreds of epigenomes. Always changing.

quiz.question: How many epigenomes does a person have?
